name: EASA on AI in aviation: the AI Roadmap 2.0 and SC-AI-01
title: EASA on AI in aviation: the AI Roadmap 2.0 and SC-AI-01
answer: EASA's research and innovation pages set out the Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0, a living action plan for safety and ethical AI in aviation, and the Final Special Condition SC-AI-01 on trustworthiness of machine learning based systems. Together they show how Europe's aviation regulator is turning AI guidance into certification material for machine learning applications.

sections.body: These pages are published by EASA, the European Union Aviation Safety Agency, on its own website under its research and innovation domain. The main page presents the EASA Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0, describing its purpose, scope and related news items. A second page is a document library entry for the Final Special Condition SC-AI-01. The pages carry no publication date in the material read, though the roadmap is described as a living document to be amended once a year.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The EASA Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 outlines the Agency's vision for the safety and ethical considerations of AI in aviation. It provides a comprehensive action plan for the EASA AI Programme and sets the pace for conceptual guidance deliverables and anticipated rulemaking activities. The roadmap also serves as a basis for discussions with all of the Agency's stakeholders, and is a living document, to be amended once a year and augmented, deepened and improved through exchanges of views and through practical work on AI development. Related news items listed on the page include the EASA Olympics for aviation AI-based systems, now closed for entries, the release of the latest issue of its Concept Paper on Artificial Intelligence for comment, the publication of the final report of the Machine Learning Application Approval Research Project, and the first public deliverable for the Machine Learning Application Approval research project. The second page covers the Final Special Condition SC-AI-01, titled Trustworthiness of Machine Learning based Systems, Issue 01, classified as important. Because the technical content was already subjected to public consultation, it will not be consulted again, and the page references the First usable guidance for Level 1 machine learning applications, Issue 01.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives few numbers. It states that the roadmap will be amended once a year, that SC-AI-01 is Issue 01 and classified as important, and that the referenced guidance is the First usable guidance for Level 1 machine learning applications, Issue 01. No traffic, safety or performance statistics appear.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader following AI in aviation, this is the regulatory record rather than commentary. The roadmap sets out the pace of conceptual guidance and anticipated rulemaking, and SC-AI-01 turns trustworthiness of machine learning based systems into a special condition, with Level 1 machine learning guidance alongside it. The related news items show the programme moving through consultation, research reports and public deliverables, which is how certification expectations for AI flight systems take shape.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Transportation

sections.body: The pages are institutional and forward looking. They describe plans, programmes and consultation status rather than results, and the roadmap is explicitly a living document subject to annual amendment. The material read gives no dates, no technical detail of the special condition itself, and no coverage of other regions or of ground transportation.
